title: Find the Lexicographically Smallest Valid Sequence
summary: Given two strings, word1 and word2, find an array of indices from word1 such that concatenating the characters at these indices in the same order results in a string that is almost equal to word2.
statement: Given two strings, word1 and word2, find an array of indices from word1 such that concatenating the characters at these indices in the same order results in a string that is almost equal to word2. The indices must be in ascending order, and the array should be the lexicographically smallest. Return an empty array if no such sequence of indices exists.
constraints: word2 is shorter than word1 and both contain lowercase letters.
Choose increasing indices spelling a length-len(word2) string that differs from word2 in at most one position.
Return the lexicographically smallest valid index list, or an empty list.
hints: A mismatch is safe only when the remaining target suffix can still be matched exactly afterward.
Precompute from the right how much of word2 remains unmatched by every word1 suffix.
Scan indices left to right, taking an exact match or the earliest feasible one-time mismatch.
Every accepted index is the smallest that preserves completion, which inductively yields the lexicographically smallest sequence.
editorial: Every accepted index is the smallest that preserves completion, which inductively yields the lexicographically smallest sequence.
